excitation_report: Typed ODE excitation compares full child vs parent systems on the q(t) trajectory. NEW term (-m_back*s*(q-q_source), the back-migration erosion feedback via state s) peaks at 6.56*sigma (max effect 0.0197 on q vs sigma=0.003), strongest at t~5.0 gen, so it clears the 5*sigma bar. Achieved by setting m_back=0.1 and beta_src=1 (tops of suggested ranges) and tau_src=5 (min of suggested range) so the erosion state s builds up quickly while the source-recipient differential is still large; effect dies as q->q_source, as physically expected. Parent terms (main migration, assortative modulation, homogenization decline via n, saturating flux) were validated in earlier generations and remain the dominant contributions.

Only data-design choices were made: time window t in [0,100] generations (captures the ~1/m~10 gen homogenization plus the slow relaxation to the asymptote), and physically sensible fixed parameters. scenario_text: Two partially isolated subpopulations exchange migrants each generation while one allele differs in frequency between them. Migration progressively homogenizes the allele frequency in the recipient population toward the source frequency. Researchers track the allele frequency in the recipient population over successive generations at a fixed migration rate. Selection and drift are treated as negligible.
